statements.text: New mental health patient; presenting after job loss, wife encouraged attendance.

evidence.quote: Honestly, my wife Samira pushed me. I got laid off six weeks ago.

statements.text: Lost job 6 weeks ago after 19 years in warehouse operations.

evidence.quote: I got laid off six weeks ago. Nineteen years at Tri-County Logistics, I ran warehouse operations

statements.text: Feels down, useless, short-tempered with children, anxious about finances.

evidence.quote: Down, mostly. Kind of useless. And I'm short with the kids

statements.text: Sleeps until 10 a.m., reduced activity, stopped Saturday basketball with friends.

evidence.quote: I sleep until 10, which I never did. I stopped going to my Saturday basketball with the guys.

statements.text: Increased appetite, mostly junk food.

evidence.quote: I'm eating more, honestly. Junk, mostly.

statements.text: No prior depressive episode or counseling ever before.

evidence.quote: No. I was fine. I've never seen a counselor or anything before this.

statements.text: Denies panic attacks or racing heart with shortness of breath; reports a knot in the stomach.

evidence.quote: Any panic attacks, or feeling like your heart is racing and you can't breathe?
No, not that. More like a knot in my stomach.

statements.text: Denies alcohol use; quit smoking 10 years ago; no other substances.

evidence.quote: What about alcohol, smoking, any other substances?
I don't drink. I smoked for years but I quit ten years ago, when my daughter was born. Nothing else.

statements.text: Denies suicidal ideation.

evidence.quote: Have you had any thoughts of ending your life, or of hurting yourself?
No. No, I'd never do that to my family.

statements.text: Denies homicidal ideation despite feeling angry.

evidence.quote: Any thoughts of hurting anyone else, maybe your old employer?
Ha, no. I'm angry, but no.

statements.text: Activities that help: walking the dog; wife supportive.

evidence.quote: What's been helping, even a little?
Walking the dog. And Samira, she's been great.

statements.text: Feels guilty that wife is picking up extra shifts.

evidence.quote: She's picking up extra shifts at the hospital, though, so I feel guilty about that too.

statements.text: Previous phone number confirmed still in use.

evidence.quote: And is 216-555-0139 still a good number for you?
Yes, that's my cell.

note.after_visit_summary: We met today and you shared what has been going on. You lost your job six weeks ago after 19 years, and since then you have felt down, worried about money, sleeping later than usual, and not doing the things you used to. Your wife encouraged you to come. We gave you two short questionnaires. Your answers showed moderate depression and moderate anxiety. Your appearance, speech, and thinking all looked fine today. We think this is an adjustment disorder, which is a strong reaction to a big life change like losing a job. It usually gets better with therapy. We will meet once a week for about an hour and use a therapy style called CBT. To start, try to get up by 7:30 on school days, spend two hours each morning looking for work, and call one basketball friend this week. Please call your employer's human resources to ask about outplacement help. Your wife can join a session later if she wants. Before you left, we started a safety plan. If you ever start thinking about hurting yourself, call or text 988 any time. If your mood gets worse even with therapy, we may talk about seeing a psychiatrist. Our next visit is next Thursday, October 1st at 4 o'clock.
